comment: Metering conformance fixture (SPEC.md 13.5, 19.2). Pins the meter event shape, the observed-meter set, the (meter, envelope_id) idempotency fold, the refusal event, and the payload.usage receipt — including a really-signed respond envelope, because the receipt's whole design is that the envelope signature covers it. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: when a test against it fails, fix the implementation; when the fixture itself is believed wrong, change it only with a spec change alongside.
spec: SPEC.md 13.5 (meters, events, receipt), 19.2 (task receipt), 19.6 (refusals rate to zero)

identities.comment: The same published test vectors budget.json, allowance.json and signature-tags.json use, deliberately: they are not real identities and control nothing, and reusing them keeps any new private-key-shaped string out of the repository. In commerce.json the sender key plays the CONSUMER OWNER (the agreement's signer); the recipient key plays the SELLING AGENT. In metering.json the sender key plays the RESPONDER (the usage receipt's signer).

observed_meters.comment: 13.5: the closed set a metering deployment MUST be able to produce. Declared meter names MUST NOT collide with these. Common declared names (SHOULD, not closed): tokens_in, tokens_out, model_ms, tool_calls.

event.comment: 13.5: quantity a non-negative integer in the meter's unit; provider and consumer always both present; envelope_id is the deriving envelope's id ((meter, envelope_id) is the idempotency key); class is 'observed' or 'declared' and is a trust statement, not a category label.

invalid.why: quantity must be an integer - a meter that needs fractions has the wrong unit
envelope_id is the idempotency key; an event without one cannot be deduplicated
both sides always: attribution in both directions is the point of the event
declared meter names MUST NOT collide with the observed set - the class is a trust statement and a collision launders a claim as an observation
a refusal event carries quantity 0 - it is a record, never a charge

idempotency.comment: 13.5: (meter, envelope_id) is the idempotency key; a consumer folding the stream MUST deduplicate on it. Same envelope_id under DIFFERENT meters is two distinct facts, not a duplicate.
idempotency.why: E1 tokens_out counted once (redelivery); E1 tool_calls is a different meter, kept; E2's second event is a duplicate KEY - first-writer wins, the 999 is dropped, exactly like the budget fixture's equal-revision rule

receipt.comment: 13.5: payload.usage on the respond - an array of {meter, quantity}. The envelope signature covers it, which is the entire design: a usage report is a signed receipt with no new signature. A non-terminal report is cumulative and SUPERSEDED by a later one, never added.

supersede_case.why: 4210, not 6210: later reports supersede earlier ones - cumulative, not additive

signed_envelope.comment: A fully-formed, really-signed terminal respond carrying payload.usage and payload.cost, generated with the published sender seed. 'canonical' is the canonical envelope JSON WITHOUT the domain prefix; the signature covers signed_bytes_prefix + canonical (SPEC.md 5.3). Any conforming implementation MUST rebuild those bytes and verify; one changed quantity must fail verification.

not_covered.comment: Boundaries, written down so nobody mistakes them for gaps.
items: Whether a declared quantity is TRUE is unverifiable by design (13.5: the signature proves authorship, not truth). This fixture pins shapes and folds, not honesty.
The task receipt's derivation (19.2) is a platform fold over these events; its wire shape is pinned by prose and unchanged from 0.2's receipt.
What a quantity COSTS is rating (19.6) - pinned in commerce.json, not here.
